evaluator: blind phase-2 evaluator (Playwright probes against build/, port 5520)
summary: Measured against build/ (bundle assets/index-Dj4VwXwL.js confirmed) with a destination tap patched onto AudioNode.connect plus a per-voice AudioBuffer tap. The DSP is genuinely strong: six audibly distinct piano types, Grand/Upright/Electric backed by 36 real WAVs each (18 roots x pp/ff, 22.05 kHz/16-bit), and Mod 1 (6/6), Mod 2 (6/6), Delay (in-loop LP/HP/BP), Amp/EQ (Twin/JC/Small/LP24/HP24), Compressor and Reverb (Booth 0.0015 -> Cathedral 0.0134 tail energy) each change rendered signal and differ from their siblings; per-unit and master bypass are bit-identical to baseline. But the browser backend bakes the chain into each voice buffer and only reverb got a live replacement: with To Rotary + ROTARY on + FAST the destination is unchanged (rms 0.04156 vs 0.04153, rmsL == rmsR exactly) and the baked buffer is bit-identical to EQ only, while the panel reports the unit engaged. Two layers never stack (1 voice per key press with A and B lit), pressing a layer button can silence the instrument, String Res is bit-identical on/off, and the declared claims for Rotary, layering, String Res, full-wet reverb and peak <= 1.0 are all contradicted by the build.

evidence: All six types measurably distinct on the per-voice rendered buffer (MIDI 60, warm library): grand rms 0.0563 / zcr 714, upright 0.0304 / 411, electric 0.0457 / 560, clav 0.0187 / 524, digital 0.0454 / 523, misc 0.0227 / 524. Pairwise envelope correlation grand|upright 0.535, grand|electric 0.705, worst-band deltas 12-38 dB; no two types share a fingerprint.

Character matches the type list: upright decays to 0.0016 by 110 ms of envelope where grand is still 0.031 and digital sustains (0.048 at 110 ms); electric shows the declared 3.93x bell partial as a band peak at ~4.5 kHz (-55 dB vs grand -88 dB).

Recorded sets are real assets, not a claim: artifact/public/samples/{grand,upright,electric} hold 36 WAVs each (mono, 22050 Hz, 16-bit, 3.2-6.0 s, 21 MB total) and the server log shows all 36 grand files fetched and decoded before the tone changes; velocity layers switch (MIDI vel 20 rms 0.0072 vs vel 127 rms 0.0906).

Simplification a player would notice: the sets are the project's own additive/physical models rendered to disk (declared honestly), so grand vs upright differ mainly in decay and brightness rather than in body resonance, and there is one model per type (the MODEL dial is decorative).

Mod 1 all six types distinct from baseline and from each other (A-Pan -1.4 dB with L/R split 0.054/0.057, Tremolo -4.5 dB, Ring Mod zcr 714 -> 1708, A-Wah -17.8 dB, Wah +6.0 dB, Pump -2.2 dB); Mod 2 all six distinct (Chorus L/R 0.044/0.065, Flanger +1.4 dB, Phaser/Vibe/Ensemble/Spin each with sibling envCorr 0.87-0.93).

Delay behaves like a delay: mix max +2.1 dB with envCorr 0.399 vs dry, feedback max +6.9 dB on top, time knob min vs max envCorr 0.327, and the feedback filter is inside the loop (LP -0.1 dB, HP -13.3 dB, BP -12.9 dB vs Off, HP vs LP -13.2 dB) while the dry onset is untouched. Reverb types decay in the documented order (mean envelope 0.6-1.2 s / 1.2-2.0 s: Booth 0.0015/0.0000, Room 0.0092/0.0000, Stage 0.0265/0.0024, Hall 0.0296/0.0097, Cathedral 0.0233/0.0134); Spring is the odd one out and BRIGHT changes the tail.

ROTARY is not connected to any audio: with amp type = To Rotary, ROTARY on and speed FAST, three repeats give destination rms 0.03971/0.04146/0.04156 vs rotary-off 0.04058/0.04153/0.04153, peak 0.2507 vs 0.2501, and rmsL == rmsR bit-for-bit (a horn/rotor would pan hard at 6.8 Hz). The connect() census over the whole session lists only Gain, Convolver, DynamicsCompressor and BufferSource edges, and the To Rotary voice buffer is bit-identical (same 32-bit fingerprint) to EQ only, because web-audio-backend.ts withoutLiveUnits() rewrites amp type 6 to 0 and forces rotary.on = false with no live replacement.

Reverb dry/wet never reaches fully wet (spec: 'fully wet at max'): the send is parallel and the dry path is never attenuated, so at AMOUNT max the direct onset is unchanged (env 0-300 ms 0.176 with reverb vs 0.170 without) and only a tail is added.
Effects are baked per voice, so engaging Mod 1 at max amount 900 ms into a held note leaves the sounding note completely unmodulated (smooth monotonic envelope 0.295 -> 0.004 across the whole hold).

One AudioContext (window counter = 1) with the documented spine: per-layer gain -> master gain -> DynamicsCompressorNode (threshold -6, ratio 16) -> single AudioDestinationNode; edge census shows exactly one DynamicsCompressorNode->AudioDestinationNode edge and no second destination. Per-unit bypass and the master Layer Effects ON are bit-identical to baseline (fingerprint match, rms delta 0.00 dB), so bypass really removes the unit.

Gain staging is not safe under load: at master max a 10-note chord peaks at 1.068 at the destination and 1.290 with amp type Small engaged (measured on the destination tap), i.e. above full scale, although the feature matrix claims 'master gain + limiter bound peaks <= 1.0'. Amp types themselves jump the bus level by +15.0 dB (Twin) and +17.8 dB (Small) before the limiter.

The reverb return bypasses the layer level stage, violating the required order (... Reverb -> Layer level -> Master): with the piano level fader at minimum the dry onset falls from 0.176 to 0.050 while the reverb tail is unchanged (0.0465 -> 0.0581 at 0.6-1.2 s, 0.0231 -> 0.0238 at 1.2-2.4 s).

The chain is not a live graph: each note-on synchronously renders 8 s of audio through the whole chain on the main thread, costing 51-97 ms per new note and blocking 268 ms for a 5-note chord, 268 ms for 10 notes and 573 ms for 10 notes with the amp engaged (performance.now around the dispatch loop). A rotaryInput GainNode is created and connected to master but nothing ever feeds it.

Two layers never sound together. With A and B both enabled (both buttons aria-pressed=true) every key press starts exactly one AudioBufferSourceNode, and the timbre is whichever layer holds focus: step 1 of the layer-logic probe gives 1 voice with the upright fingerprint (rms 0.0304 / zcr 411) while layer A (grand) is still on. engine.noteOn() routes only to focusedLayer, so a stacked A+B piano is unreachable.

Pressing a layer button can silence the instrument: pressing B when B is on leaves A enabled but produces 0 voices and no sound (step 3), and pressing A when A is on with B enabled likewise gives 0 voices (step 6). Sync moves focus to the enabled layer and pressFunctionalControl then moves it back to the layer just disabled; the dead state persists until some other control is touched.

The single type button always rewrites the focused layer: after setting B to Electric, pressing any functional control (fx.effect1On) made B sound bit-identical to clean Grand again (same fingerprint as A.clean), so a Grand-A / Electric-B setup cannot survive panel use. The type LED also disagrees with what is sounding (panel reads 'Grand' while layer B renders Electric at rms 0.0457 / zcr 560).

What does work: octave shift transposes the focused layer (zcr 560 -> 1181 for +12, -> 296 for -12), the level fader scales the mix (min rms 0.0083 vs max 0.0939), each layer keeps its own effect chain, and the Program OLED tracks focus and model ('Piano A: Grand Lady D' -> 'Piano B: Grand Upright'). But the level fader writes both layers at once (panel-bindings.ts sets pianoA and pianoB from piano.level), and FX focus does not follow layer focus: with layer B focused, a Mod 1 edit landed on chain A and left the sounding layer bit-identical to clean.

Five of six controls measurably change rendered audio and behave like their namesakes: KB Touch Light +1.59 dB / Heavy -1.81 dB vs Medium; Dyn Comp raises only soft strokes (soft +2.44 / +4.42 / +6.10 dB at 1/2/3 while the same hard strike moves +0.10 / +0.19 / +0.27 dB), which is exactly the manual's 'narrows dynamic range'; Timbre Soft/Mid/Bright differ by 14-21 dB of band energy and from each other; Unison 1/2/3 each differ (sibling envCorr 0.927 and 0.944, stereo peak 0.464 -> 0.588).
Soft Release measured on the destination tap after key-up: envelope at 700 ms 0.0210 with it on vs 0.0022 off, at 1000 ms 0.0051 vs 0.0000.

String Res does nothing in the shipped build. The voice buffer is bit-identical with it on and off (same fingerprint, rms delta 0.00 dB), and a two-note held test differs by only -0.05 dB rms / envCorr 0.987 - inside the capture noise floor measured between identical repeats (envCorr 0.956). render.ts only adds resonance when a single render holds >= 2 voices, and the browser renders one voice per buffer, so the declared 'simulated sympathetic-resonance wash' never reaches the output.

Timbre panel feedback lies on acoustic types: the button cycles six options, and selecting 'Dyno 1' or 'Dyno 2' on the Grand renders bit-identical to Off and to Soft respectively (panel-bindings.ts takes timbre modulo 4 for non-electric types) while the LED shows the Dyno position.

All three input paths reach one note lifecycle. Pointer: a real mouse press on a key sounds and velocity follows strike height (rms 0.0131 near the top vs 0.0846 at the front edge). Computer keyboard: mapped keys play and space sustains (tail rms 0.0019 1.1 s after key-up with the pedal down vs 0.0000 without), and SUSTPED off correctly stops the pedal reaching the layer (rms 0.0000). MIDI (stubbed requestMIDIAccess, since headless reports 'denied'): status reads 'MIDI: ready', note-on plays, velocity 20 vs 127 gives rms 0.0072 vs 0.0906, and CC64 holds (0.0066) then releases (0.0000).

Polyphony and cleanup hold under stress: 24 simultaneous keys settle to exactly 16 live sources per layer with deterministic stealing and return to 0 after release; PANIC while 7 notes are held gives destination rms 0.0000; Piano ON off produces 0 voices; no console errors during the whole interaction pass.

Failure does not degrade gracefully: blocking ./samples/** produces the correct labeled fallback ('Synthesized fallback: grand samples failed to load') and the type stays playable (1 voice, rms 0.0454), but the retry path is unbounded - markTypeFailed -> pushConfig -> configure -> ensureLibrary -> fail loops, and the page logged 182,120 console errors / unhandled 'Failed to fetch' rejections in about 15 s.

Input latency is poor under chords because every new note synchronously renders 8 s of audio: the dispatch of 22 key-downs blocked the main thread for 499 ms, and a 10-note chord blocks 268 ms (573 ms with the amp engaged), so held-key input and UI updates stall audibly.

All six required types are selectable from the panel type button and all six produce audio (measured fingerprints for grand/upright/electric/clav/digital/misc, each unique); the three recorded types actually load over HTTP (36 x 200 responses per set in the server log) and the Program OLED names the model live ('Piano A: Grand Lady D', 'Piano A: Sparkle Top', 'Piano B: Grand Upright').

Provenance in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json matches the artifact byte for byte: 18 declared root notes x pp/ff x 3 types = 108 files, and artifact/public/samples holds exactly that, mono 22050 Hz 16-bit as declared, with scripts/render-samples.mjs present as the stated generator; nothing is described as third-party audio.

Loading/failure state is truthful when it fails (labeled synthesized fallback, still playable), though the status bar already reads 'ready (recorded sample library)' before any library is decoded - the first note after page load measurably renders the fallback voice (cold rms 0.0454 / zcr 523 vs warm 0.0563 / 714 for the same key).

Gaps against the piano spec: one model per type and a decorative MODEL dial (optional in the spec), and the focused layer's type is silently overwritten by the single panel type value on every functional control press, so per-layer instrument assignment is not stable.

The whole unit inventory is present and panel-reachable in the effects section (38 controls enumerated from the DOM): Mod 1 (6 types, rate, amount, on), Mod 2 (6 types, rate, amount, on), Delay (rate, feedback, mix, tap, ping-pong, 4-way filter, global, on), Amp Sim/EQ (7 types incl. To Rotary, drive, bass/mid/treble, on), Compressor (amount, fast, global, on), Reverb (6 types, amount, bright, global, on), Rotary (on, slow/fast, drive), plus Layer Effects ON, A/B focus and GROUP.

Reachability is behavioural, not decorative: 25 of the 26 listed types measurably alter rendered audio and differ from their siblings, per-unit ON is bit-exact bypass, and global mode works across chains (delay set global on chain B changed layer A's rendered voice, envCorr 0.616 vs clean).

Missing or inert coverage: the Rotary unit processes nothing (see effectAudibility), the To Rotary amp type is bit-identical to EQ only, the spec's manual focus buttons for Organ/Piano/Synth do not exist (only A/B; focusSection is hard-coded to 'piano'), there is no separate Mid Freq control (fx.eqMidGain drives both mid gain and mid frequency in panel-bindings.ts), and ping-pong renders bit-identical output because the layer source is mono.

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json states 'Reverb and Rotary run live in the browser so mixes stay correct' and 'reverb always precedes rotary'. Measured: reverb does run live (convolver send), Rotary does not exist in the browser graph at all - no rotary node in the connect census, To Rotary bit-identical to EQ only, destination unchanged with ROTARY on and FAST.

tests/feature-matrix.json declares as covered several behaviours the build contradicts: 'two types sound together' (measured 1 voice per key press with both layers on), 'String Res (sympathetic energy while held)' (bit-identical buffers), 'Rotary (slow/fast distinct, drive)' (no change at the destination), 'master gain + limiter bound peaks <= 1.0' (measured destination peaks 1.068 and 1.290), and 'Reverb ... fully wet at max' (dry onset unchanged at max). These hold in the offline renderGraph the tests exercise but not in the WebAudioBackend the user hears.

What is declared accurately: the decorative boundary (organ drawbar to 8, organ model cycled, synth ON pressed - 0 voices started, keybed still plays only piano), sample provenance and file inventory, per-layer SUSTPED gating, 16-voice polyphony with deterministic stealing, and the labeled fallback on asset failure - each verified in the running build.
Nothing is declared unimplemented that actually works, so the inaccuracy is one-directional: the artifact over-claims rather than under-claims.

issues.title: Rotary is disconnected from the audio path while the panel reports it engaged
issues.detail: With amp type To Rotary, ROTARY on and speed FAST, the destination capture is unchanged from rotary-off (rms 0.04156 vs 0.04153, peak 0.2507 vs 0.2501, rmsL identical to rmsR to full precision - a horn/rotor would pan hard at 6.8 Hz). The per-voice buffer with To Rotary is bit-identical to EQ only, and the AudioNode.connect census contains no rotary DSP node; web-audio-backend.ts withoutLiveUnits() rewrites amp type 6 to 0 and sets rotary.on = false, and the rotaryInput GainNode it creates is never fed. The panel LED, the visual audit and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS all report a working Rotary. This is the honesty-contract failure the phase gates on: a claimed audio feature not connected to the audible signal graph.

issues.title: Two piano layers never stack, and a layer button can leave the instrument silent
issues.detail: Both layer buttons lit still produces exactly one voice per key press (engine.noteOn routes only to focusedLayer), so the Phase 2 outcome 'two piano layers' is unreachable - measured as 1 AudioBufferSourceNode start and the focused layer's fingerprint. Worse, pressing a lit layer button disables that layer AND moves focus to it (syncFunctionalControls corrects focus, then pressFunctionalControl overrides it), so the keybed goes completely silent with the other layer enabled and lit: 0 voices measured after pressing B (A still on) and again after pressing A (B still on). Recovery only happens when some other functional control is touched.

issues.title: String Res is inert in the built app
issues.detail: The rendered voice buffer is bit-identical with String Res on and off (identical fingerprint, 0.00 dB rms delta), and a two-note held comparison differs by less than the measured capture noise. render.ts adds sympathetic resonance only when one render contains two or more held voices, but the Web Audio backend renders each voice in its own single-note render, so the control - declared functional and asserted by the offline tests - can never change what the user hears.

issues.title: Declared coverage describes the offline renderer, not the shipped backend
issues.detail: Five feature-matrix/IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS claims are contradicted by measurement of build/: Rotary live in the browser, 'two types sound together', String Res sympathetic energy, 'limiter bound peaks <= 1.0' (measured 1.068 and 1.290 at the destination), and reverb 'fully wet at max' (dry onset unchanged at max). All five hold in the deterministic offline renderGraph the unit tests exercise; the WebAudioBackend diverges from it (per-voice baking, reverb replaced by a parallel send, rotary dropped) and nothing in the declaration records that divergence.

issues.title: Sample-load failure triggers an unbounded fetch retry storm
issues.detail: Aborting requests to ./samples/** yields the correct labeled fallback and a playable voice, but markTypeFailed -> pushConfig -> configure -> ensureLibrary re-issues the failed load on every state push with no failure memo: the page logged 182,120 console errors and unhandled 'Failed to fetch' rejections in roughly 15 s. The degradation is visible but it also floods the console and the network indefinitely.

issues.title: Per-note synchronous rendering blocks the main thread, and loud amp types push the bus over full scale
issues.detail: Each new note+config combination renders 8 s of audio through the whole chain on the main thread: 51-97 ms per note, 268 ms for a 5- or 10-note chord, 573 ms for a 10-note chord with the amp engaged, 499 ms to dispatch 22 key-downs. Separately, amp types raise the bus level by +15.0 dB (Twin) and +17.8 dB (Small) before the DynamicsCompressor limiter, and the destination peaks at 1.068 (10 notes, no amp) and 1.290 (10 notes + Small) with master at maximum.

issues.title: The focused layer's piano type is overwritten by the single panel value on every control press
issues.detail: syncFunctionalControls writes the panel type into engine.setLayerType(focusedLayer, ...) on every functional control change. After selecting Electric on layer B, pressing an unrelated effects control made B render bit-identical to clean Grand. The type LED also shows the panel value rather than the focused layer's model, so panel feedback and sounding voice disagree (panel 'Grand' while layer B renders Electric).

issues.title: Reverb return bypasses the layer level stage and never reaches fully wet
issues.detail: The reverb send is tapped from the per-voice gain and returns straight to master, so with the piano level fader at minimum the dry onset drops from 0.176 to 0.050 while the tail rises slightly (0.0465 -> 0.0581 at 0.6-1.2 s), and at maximum AMOUNT the dry path is never attenuated (spec: 'Dry/Wet (fully wet at max)').

issues.title: Effect edits never affect sounding notes
issues.detail: Because the chain is baked into each voice buffer, engaging Mod 1 at maximum amount 900 ms into a held note left the note's envelope perfectly smooth and unmodulated. On the hardware every unit is live on held notes; here only reverb send level, layer level and master level ride real nodes.

issues.title: Timbre shows Dyno 1/2 on acoustic types but applies Off/Soft
issues.detail: The timbre button always cycles six options; on the Grand, 'Dyno 1' renders bit-identical to Off and 'Dyno 2' identical to Soft (timbre is taken modulo 4 for non-electric types), so two of six LED positions report a setting the engine does not apply.

issues.title: FX focus does not follow layer focus and the section focus buttons are absent
issues.detail: The effects spec requires focus to follow layer focus plus manual Organ/Piano/Synth focus buttons. Only A/B focus buttons exist and focusSection is hard-coded to 'piano'; with layer B focused, a Mod 1 edit landed on chain A and the sounding layer stayed bit-identical to clean. Neither focus button shows a default pressed state on load.

issues.title: Status reads 'ready (recorded sample library)' before any library is decoded
issues.detail: The engine reports ready at init while the recorded libraries are still fetching, so the first note after page load renders the synthesized fallback (cold rms 0.0454 / zcr 523 vs warm 0.0563 / 714 for the same key) under a status line that already claims the recorded library.

notes: Measured against build/ served by python3 -m http.server on 127.0.0.1:5520; the page loaded assets/index-Dj4VwXwL.js, matching build/assets. Probes drove the real page with Playwright (real mouse for pointer velocity, page.keyboard for keys, focus + Enter/Home/End/PageUp one event per animation frame for panel controls); audio was measured two ways - a per-voice tap on AudioBufferSourceNode.start (deterministic, captures everything baked into the voice: Mod 1/2, Delay, Amp/EQ, Compressor, timbre, unison, KB Touch, Dyn Comp, String Res) and a ScriptProcessor tap patched onto AudioNode.connect at ctx.destination (captures reverb, rotary, layer level, master level, sustain tails). A warm-up note plus a 6-7 s library wait preceded every instrument measurement, since the first note after load renders the fallback. Real-time capture noise floor was established by repeating an identical capture (rms delta 0.00 dB, envCorr 0.956), and every live-path conclusion is stated relative to it. Web MIDI reported 'denied' in headless Chromium, so the MIDI path was exercised through a stubbed navigator.requestMIDIAccess; the MIDI results above are measured through that stub, not through a real device. The four technical checks were not re-run from a clean install - they are taken from inputs/verification.json (test/typecheck/lint/build all passed at seal). Phase 2 is judged-only, so no computed criteria appear here and no measurements object was filled.
